divergences.old: Kibana used the Elasticsearch API key whenever it had none of its own: PNCLI_KIBANA_API_KEY, then PNCLI_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY, then the stored kibana.apiKey, then the stored elasticsearch.apiKey
divergences.toil: A Kibana connection uses an Elasticsearch connection's apiKey only when it names it in apiKeyFrom, with the env tier beating the file tier and Kibana's own key winning a tie. The one exception keeps the old env chain: Kibana's default connection takes TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY when TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY isn't set. A stored Elasticsearch key is never borrowed unpaired. The key still goes only to the Kibana connection's own baseUrl, and meta.context.shared says when it was borrowed
divergences.why: Cross-area credentials need an explicit pairing (maintainer decision 7 on #68): a credential goes only to the connection it's configured on, or to one the user paired it with.

divergences.old: With no key: "Kibana credentials not configured. Set kibana.apiKey, or elasticsearch.apiKey to share the Elasticsearch key."
divergences.toil: NOT_CONFIGURED, "Kibana credentials not configured on connection <name>.", with a fix naming TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY, toil connections login and the apiKeyFrom pairing; nothing is sent
divergences.why: The old advice is no longer true: a stored elasticsearch.apiKey is shared only through apiKeyFrom, so the error says what does work.
